Delay Controller

Delay Controller coordinates time-based execution control by deterministically pausing pipeline progression for a fixed interval before allowing a state update attempt to proceed.

This controller operates within the Policy stage and does not observe, derive, or modify state values. Instead, it acts as an execution authority that controls when a candidate update is allowed to continue through the pipeline.

When an update attempt enters the pipeline, the Delay Controller may temporarily suspend execution by issuing a pause decision. Once the configured delay interval has elapsed, the controller explicitly releases the suspended attempt, allowing normal pipeline execution to resume.

The Delay Controller does not suppress, coalesce, or transform updates. Every update attempt is preserved and resumes execution unchanged after the delay expires. The controller’s sole responsibility is to enforce a deterministic, time-based pause before pipeline continuation.

Note

The Delay Controller governs execution timing, not value admission or derivation. It does not participate in filtering, reduction, or resolution logic, and it does not enqueue or drop candidate values. Its authority is limited strictly to pausing and resuming pipeline execution based Flowon elapsed time.

Diagrams
Configuration

The Delay Controller introduces a fixed, deterministic pause in pipeline execution for each state update attempt. When an update enters the pipeline, execution is suspended for the configured interval before the attempt is allowed to continue.

The controller operates at the execution level rather than the value level. It does not modify, suppress, merge, or inspect candidate values. Each update attempt is paused and resumed independently, preserving value integrity and execution ordering.

Unlike debounce or throttle mechanisms, the Delay Controller does not collapse, skip, or replace updates. Every update attempt is eventually released after its delay elapses, ensuring that no state transitions are implicitly dropped or coalesced.

This controller is commonly used to stage state transitions, coordinate UI timing or animations, simulate network latency, or align pipeline execution with external temporal constraints.

The delay duration is supplied explicitly during FeatureCell definition. The Delay Controller is configured once, remains active for the lifetime of the FeatureCell, and applies uniformly to all update attempts processed by the pipeline.

Configuration Option
Property Description
millisecondDelay: number Fixed delay duration, in milliseconds, applied to each pipeline execution attempt before continuation is permitted. Must be a valid, non-negative number.
Registering the Delay Controller

The Delay Controller is attached structurally when the FeatureCell is defined. This determines that the FeatureCell participates in delay-based execution control at runtime.

Registering the controller does not configure delay controller by itself. It enables the controller so that delay options supplied later via the fluent API can be applied during pipeline execution.

Once attached, delay behavior is configured using the fluent API during initialization via .withDelay(<WithDelayControllerOptions>). 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {  
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [],
      },
      [
        // Optional add-on behaviors
      ],
      [
        // Attach the Delay Controller structurally
        withDelayController
      ]
    )
  ]
};
`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Optional add-on behaviors
  ],
  [
    // Attach the Delay Controller structurally
    withDelayController
  ]
);`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',

Delay Execution Timeline

The table below illustrates how the Delay Controller applies a fixed delay of 1000 milliseconds to each pipeline execution attempt. Every incoming attempt is accepted immediately but paused deterministically until its individual delay interval has elapsed. No attempts are suppressed, merged, or reordered.

Delay Controller — Execution Example (1000ms)
Attempt Delayed Attempt Time (ms) Controller Outcome Policy Vote
1 0 Gated
resumes at t = 1000 		Deny
2 250 Gated
resumes at t = 1250 		Deny
3 500 Gated
resumes at t = 1500 		Deny
4 750 Gated
resumes at t = 1750 		Deny
5 1000 Gated
resumes at t = 2000 		Deny
1 1000 Allowed
enters pipeline at t = 1000 		Abstain
2 1250 Allowed
enters pipeline at t = 1250 		Abstain
3 1500 Allowed
enters pipeline at t = 1500 		Abstain
4 1750 Allowed
enters pipeline at t = 1750 		Abstain
5 2000 Allowed
enters pipeline at t = 2000 		Abstain

Each attempt is paused independently and released precisely when its delay expires. The Delay Controller issues a pause vote during the delay window and abstains once the execution is eligible to resume.

Examples

Delay is enabled by attaching the Delay Controller via the fluent API during FeatureCell initialization. Each incoming update is admitted into pipeline execution only after the configured delay interval has elapsed.

Because delay is implemented as a controller, it coordinates when pipeline execution proceeds without suppressing, coalescing, or modifying state values.

Example 1: Configure a FeatureCell with Delay

In this example, every incoming state update is delayed by 500 milliseconds before pipeline execution begins. All updates are forwarded independently after the delay interval. 

{{`
@FeatureCell<Employee[][]>('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[][]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Apply delay controller configuration during initialization
    this.vault
      .withDelay?.({
        millisecondDelay: 500
      })
      .initialize();
  }
}
`}}
 
{{`
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
    [
      // Additional add-on behaviors
    ],
    [
      withDelayController
    ]
  }
);

// Apply delay controller configuration during initialization
employeeCell
  .withDelay?.({
    millisecondDelay: 500
  })
  .initialize();
`}}
 
{{`
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
    [
      // Additional add-on behaviors
    ],
    [
      withDelayController
    ]
  }
);

// Apply delay controller configuration during initialization
employeeCell
  .withDelay?.({
    millisecondDelay: 500
  })
  .initialize();
`}}

In all cases, the Delay Controller pauses pipeline execution for each update trace independently and resumes execution only after the configured delay has elapsed. No updates are dropped, merged, or reordered.
